<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
          <jats:p>
            We evaluated the MIC Strip Isavuconazole test against EUCAST E.Def 9.3 by using 40 wild-type and 39
            <jats:italic>CYP51A</jats:italic>
            mutant
            <jats:named-content content-type="genus-species">Aspergillus fumigatus</jats:named-content>
            strains. The strip full inhibition endpoint (FIE) and 80% growth inhibition endpoint were determined by two independent readers, reader 1 (R1) and R2. The essential (within ±0, ±1, and ±2 twofold dilutions) and categorical agreements were best with the FIE (for R1/R2, 42%/41%, 75%/73%, and 90%/89% for essential agreement, and 91.1%/92.4% categorical agreement, with 6.3/8.9% very major errors and 0/1.3% major errors, respectively). The MIC Strip Isavuconazole test with the FIE appears to be useful.
          </jats:p>
title: Evaluation of MIC Strip Isavuconazole Test for Susceptibility Testing of Wild-Type and Non-Wild-Type Aspergillus fumigatus Isolates

items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">The article begins by examining the artistic effects of a formal device, narrative iteration, which consists in presenting the same events twice or more times. As an example from Tolstoy’s Anna Karenina shows, this kind of recounting has important artistic consequences: within the story’s plot it emphasizes the characters’ feelings and responses, thus offering the readers elements that naturally attract human attention: passions, conflicts, options, and decisions, in particular spectacular, risky decisions. Asserting that for a long time successful narratives were built around worthy topics of gossip and/or news—couple formation, individual violations of law, and fights between nations—the article argues that in twentieth-century high literature attractive, well-organized plots are less frequent, the main modes of modernist literary attention being a dispersal of attention that encourages detachment from the world and a self-involvement that entails an endless wandering within one’s own inner depths. These two kinds of narrative attention, one naturally focused on human actions and passions, the other one turning away from them, either through dispersion or self-examination, shape the way in which readers relate to the world of the story, sympathize with its characters, and participate in it. Based on Jonathan Lear’s theory of catharsis, the article concludes that “gossip/news” narratives induce a significant amount of empathy, while narratives of dispersal and self-involvement often fail to do so.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Voice interfaces to anthropomorphic robotic arms have typically been evaluated without a formal safety layer, or with safety implemented as a post-hoc filter around a transcript the filter must trust — approaches that leave the case of a corrupted transcript, common under non-native speech, unaddressed. This paper presents the DAS3 Neuro-Voice Controller, a voice-driven pipeline for a musculoskeletal arm model built around three commitments. First, intent classification is performed by a compact fine-tuned on-device transformer — a 44 M-parameter DistilBERT classifier over a bounded nine-command vocabulary — rather than a cloud generative model. Second, safety is enforced by a deterministic three-layer Gatekeeper covering semantic validation, kinematic feasibility, and hard safety constraints, independently of classifier confidence. Third, an upstream Phonetic Interceptor sanitises characteristic automatic speech recognition mutilations of anatomical and safety terms ("four arm" → "forearm") before any downstream component can act on them. The system was trained on a class-balanced adversarial corpus of 3,591 expressions and evaluated on a fourteen-participant live-pipeline cohort of non-native English speakers. The classifier reached 99.95 % top-1 accuracy across 1,847 oracle-resolvable utterances; the Gatekeeper reduced a previously observed Priority Override Failure rate to 0.0 %, rejected 100 % of out-of-domain speech, and held false-rejection on valid input at 2.02 %. Against a strict keyword-spotter baseline the pipeline delivered a 17.4-fold improvement in end-to-end success. The acoustic front-end is the principal residual weakness — locatable and contained. Upstream input repair and downstream deterministic gating emerge as first-class components of safety-critical voice interfaces for assistive systems.</jats:p>
title: Hearing It Right, Doing It Safely: An On-Device Small-Language-Model Architecture for Voice-Controlled Assistive Manipulation
